hero.headline: Florida Brewery Closes After Nearly Five Years in Business
hero.body:

The closure affects employees who worked at the facility and customers who frequented the establishment. The brewery had been serving the local community since it opened approximately five years ago. The business cited challenges in sustaining operations as the reason for shutting down.

The closure adds to the ongoing changes in Florida's craft brewery industry. Many small breweries face pressure from larger competitors and changing consumer preferences. The business had attempted to build a customer base over its years of operation but ultimately could not continue.

The former brewery location will remain closed as owners determine next steps for the property. Local residents who supported the brewery will need to find alternative locations for craft beer. The closure represents a loss for the local business community and those employed at the facility.

cards.headline: Martin County Man Sues Sheriff's Office After Database Error Led to 14 Days in Jail
cards.body:
A Martin County man filed a lawsuit against the Martin County Sheriff's Office after a database error resulted in his wrongful detention for two weeks. The man was arrested and held in jail for 14 days on a felony charge that officials say stemmed from an error in the law enforcement database system.

The lawsuit claims the Sheriff's Office failed to properly verify information in its database before making the arrest. The man spent two weeks in custody before officials discovered the mistake and released him. The database error that triggered the arrest has raised concerns about the accuracy of law enforcement record systems used throughout Martin County.

The plaintiff is seeking damages for the time he spent wrongfully incarcerated and the impact the arrest had on his life. The lawsuit alleges negligence on the part of the Martin County Sheriff's Office for relying on faulty database information without adequate verification procedures. Legal experts say cases involving database errors can result in significant liability for law enforcement agencies when proper protocols are not followed.

The Martin County Sheriff's Office has not publicly commented on the pending litigation. The case highlights ongoing concerns about the reliability of criminal justice databases and the procedures law enforcement agencies use to confirm warrant information before making arrests. The outcome of this lawsuit could have implications for how the Sheriff's Office and other local agencies verify database information in the future.

The Tigers reached the semifinals after staging a comeback victory in regional play. Martin County will compete in the Class 6A state semifinal, representing the first time the school has advanced this far in state competition since 1968. Both Martin County and Vero Beach high schools advanced to their respective state semifinals on the same day.

The semifinal appearance represents a significant milestone for Martin County High School athletics. The team's advancement breaks a drought that has lasted nearly six decades, dating back to the school's last state tournament run in the late 1960s. The state semifinal game will determine whether Martin County advances to the state championship. Vero Beach High School also advanced to its state semifinal in a separate classification, giving the Treasure Coast two teams competing at the state level simultaneously. The commission meeting comes after previous discussions on establishing quiet zones at railroad crossings in Martin County. In March 2025, county leaders voted down a proposal for quiet zones at railroad crossings. Train horn regulations typically require locomotives to sound their horns at public crossings to warn motorists and pedestrians. Establishing quiet zones requires communities to implement additional safety measures at crossings, which can include upgraded crossing gates, medians, and other infrastructure improvements. The process involves coordination with railroad companies and federal transportation authorities.
